overall:
Release run with sonnet on `0.5.x` at `26f8943` (skforecast 0.27.0): 48 sessions, the 12 scenarios with the skill and the 4 of the ablation, 3 repetitions. 46 correct, 2 improvable, 0 fail. No critical scenario fails in any repetition and no session without the skill fails. No confirmed invented figure: the numbers without a source are the mean 1.2922255 the user asked for (right), row counts read from the file and example horizons. No file of the user modified (hash check 48 of 48), nothing written nor attempted before the user agreed (12 of 12 two-turn sessions), no model switched without telling (the 14 sessions that forecast with Chronos-2 name it with the license of the notice; `exog_no_future__r3` forecasts with the baseline that won and says so; the 2 sessions that change Ridge for RandomForestRegressor say so and why), no error retried in a loop (48 of 48).

**Inconclusive, 10 of the 12 `dirty_data` and `dirty_data_keep_gaps` sessions**: `dirty_data__r1`, `__r2`, `__r3`, `dirty_data__noskill__r1`, `__noskill__r2`, `__noskill__r3`, `dirty_data_keep_gaps__r1`, `__r2`, `__r3` and `dirty_data_keep_gaps__noskill__r2`. In each, the shell command that writes the corrected copy after the user agreed is denied by the client (8 for an output redirection into `data/`, 2 for a here-document that writes a script under `/tmp`); the denial text of Claude Code says `do not retry it: this action, and anything else that requires approval, will be denied the same way`, and the agent stops and tells the user. None tries `Write`, which the scenario allows. The failed checks on the copy are a limit of the harness, not a result, and are not counted; the verdict is that of what can be judged (the first answer names the three problems and asks in 12 of 12, no write before the agreement, no value filled or invented, an honest account of the denial with the command or the rows for the user): correct in the 10. The 2 sessions that complete, `dirty_data_keep_gaps__noskill__r1` and `__noskill__r3`, write with `python3` and no redirection; both copies are right (one `2002-09-01` row, `2006-01-01,1.2922255`, no row for 2001-01, 2001-02 nor 2004-10; checked in `artifacts/`).

**1. Missing values (D38).** What this run shows rests on those 2 sessions, both without the skill; no session with the skill gets past the error of `profile`. All 12 receive the `invalid_argument` of `profile` (1 date with two values, 1 identical repeated row, 3 timestamps missing at `MS`). The 2 that go on receive: the `DataProfileWarning` of the 3 missing timestamps in `profile` and `plan`; with Ridge, `MissingValuesNotice` plus a `UserWarning` in `create_cv`, then `invalid_argument` from `backtest` (`To predict 1 of the 3 test folds, the forecaster reads values of the target before the start of those folds ... ('x': 1 value(s), such as '2004-10-01')`, naming RandomForestRegressor); with RandomForestRegressor, `create_cv` has 0 notices (2 of 2, the new behavior) and `backtest` runs with a `UserWarning` and an `EstimatorNotRecommendedNotice`. Both read it right: `one fold depends on the missing month 2004-10-01` and `the gap at 2004-10-01 feeds one test fold`; 0 of 2 place the value inside a fold, 0 say anything false about what was measured (36 of 36 predictions), 2 of 2 say that the estimator changed and why. 0 of 12 sessions fill or invent a value; 1 first answer names interpolation as an option for the user to choose. The count `1 of the 3 test folds` was reproduced outside the session with skforecast 0.27.0 on the copy of the session: only the first fold fails with Ridge (`lag_11` at step 3). Not exercised by this run: a missing target value inside a test fold, left out of the metrics and counted by the summary. The three missing months of `h2o_dirty` are all before the first test fold (2005-07), so `n_evaluated` is 36 of 36; neither session runs `compare` on the copy, so `no baseline with gaps` is not exercised either.

**2. Restricted models.** `restricted_model`: 3 of 3 stop after `model_not_allowed`, run nothing, quote the license from the message of the error (`timesfm-non-commercial-license-v1.0`, with its link) and offer only the default model with the license of the hint. `foundation_default`: 3 of 3 run Chronos-2 with the license of the `ModelLicenseNotice`. 0 of 48 sessions name Timestral, TiRex-2, Moirai, TabPFN or TS-ICL, so the new entry of the skill and the default permission of TiRex-2 were not exercised: nobody asks for those models.

**3. Requirements of `get_code`.** 3 sessions call it (4 calls, all `compare_code`); the response gives `pandas==2.3.3`, `skforecast==0.27.0`, `chronos-forecasting==2.3.2` and the 3 answers quote exactly that, as one `pip install` line. A backend with extras does not appear in these responses: unverified.

**4. MASE.** 17 sessions quote a value; 16 give a reading, all against the one-step naive forecast (repeat the previous value), and 0 against the seasonal naive baseline row; `compare_code__r1` lists the column without a reading. None says `on the training data`, none quotes the new wording.

**5. One `MissingValuesWarning`.** The 3 forecasts on the copy with gaps (2 sessions) carry exactly one, with counts: Ridge `69 of 84 rows are dropped: 1 with a NaN target and 68 with NaN predictors`, RandomForestRegressor `1 of 84 rows is dropped (NaN target) and 68 are kept with NaN predictors`. `dirty_data_keep_gaps__noskill__r3` quotes the counts right; `__noskill__r1` only says the model trains on rows with missing values.

**Also denied by the client**: `err_url__r1` and `__r3` never reach the server (their download command starts with a shell variable and one of its parts needs approval); both ask the user for the file, which the scenario accepts, and `err_url__r2` downloads and forecasts. Kinds of the model already logged recur: an interval or a metric list nobody asked for (9 sessions), the bounds of the forecast described from their means (4), the short last fold missed with several series (3 of 3, from 2 of 3) and a cause of its own for a metric (2).

findings.title: The changes for missing values (D38) are seen by 2 of 12 sessions, none with the skill, and the data of the scenario cannot exercise a missing value inside a test fold.
findings.evidence: 10 of the 12 `dirty_data` and `dirty_data_keep_gaps` sessions end at a denied shell command after the user agreed to the copy: `sed '91d' ... > h2o_clean.csv` (dirty_data__r1, dirty_data__noskill__r1), `awk ... > h2o_clean.csv` (dirty_data__r2, dirty_data__noskill__r2, dirty_data__noskill__r3, dirty_data_keep_gaps__r1, dirty_data_keep_gaps__r2, dirty_data_keep_gaps__noskill__r2) and `mkdir -p /tmp/fixscript && cat > ... <<'EOF'` (dirty_data__r3, dirty_data_keep_gaps__r3). The denial text read in the traces: `Output redirection to '<ws>/data/h2o_clean.csv' needs approval ... do not retry it: this action, and anything else that requires approval, will be denied the same way for the rest of this session`. The 10 agents obey it and stop; 0 of 10 try `Write`, which is allowed. The 2 that complete call `python3 -I` without a redirection. So 6 of 6 sessions with the skill never reach `plan`, `create_cv` nor `backtest`. Besides, in `h2o_dirty` the missing months are 2001-01, 2001-02 and 2004-10 and the first test fold starts in 2005-07: the backtests of the 2 complete sessions score 36 of 36 predictions, so no session can show a test date left out of the metrics nor the count the summary gives for it. Rate of denied writes: 10 of 12, from 4 of 6 `dirty_data` in `0.5.0-fix2-haiku` (accepted in the log as model and harness).
findings.action: Nothing in the server. To get evidence for D38 before the release: in the harness, let a session write inside its own `data/` (a permission that allows redirections there, or a second turn that names the file tool), or accept the 2 complete sessions as the evidence; and add a dataset with a missing month inside the last 30 % of the series, the only way a session meets a test date left out of the metrics. Optional in the skill, as proposed in `0.5.0-fix2-haiku`: say that the agreed copy is written with the file tool of the client.

findings.title: On the copy with three missing months, the forecast of the recommended Ridge plan trains on 15 of 84 rows, and nothing but the counts of the notice says so.
findings.evidence: dirty_data_keep_gaps__noskill__r1, call 7: `forecast` of the recommended plan (ForecasterRecursive, Ridge, lags 1, 11, 12, 13, windows 3, 12 and 36) runs and returns predictions with `MissingValuesWarning: 69 of 84 rows are dropped: 1 with a NaN target and 68 with NaN predictors`; the plan only says `NaN rows will be dropped before fitting`. Reproduced outside the session with skforecast 0.27.0 on the copy of the session (`create_train_X_y` with `dropna_from_series=True`): 15 of 84 rows kept for 8 lag and window predictors (calendar features aside); without the window of 36, 78 of 107; on the first training window of the backtest, 7 of 48. The same check shows why: when training, a rolling window that holds one missing value gives a missing predictor (the 68 rows), while when predicting the rolling statistics skip it (folds 2 and 3 predict without NaN from a window that holds 2004-10). The agent of that session does not quote the counts; it discards that forecast for another reason (not measured). In dirty_data_keep_gaps__noskill__r3 the Ridge plan is never forecast. A session that forecasts without a backtest, as 2 of 3 `exog_no_future__noskill` do, would hand over that forecast with only the unmeasured notice. 1 of the 2 sessions that reach it; new with the single notice of point 5, which is where the counts now are.
findings.action: Decide whether it is enough. Options: the notice of the forecast (and the note of the plan) could say how many rows are left to train on and warn when most are dropped, naming the window feature that causes it; or the difference between training and prediction of the rolling features with missing values goes upstream as a skforecast issue. Informational: no answer of this run gave the user that forecast as reliable.

findings.title: A cause of its own for a metric: the MAPE of 168 % is said to be inflated by hours with few users.
findings.evidence: exog_no_future__r1 (skill): `The mean absolute percentage error is 1.68, meaning 168%. That figure is inflated by hours with very few users.` exog_no_future__noskill__r3: `MAPE: 1.68, which is 168%. It is inflated by hours with very low user counts.` No response says it: the `MetricUnitNotice` only gives the conversion, and rule 7 of the instructions and the skill forbid a cause for a metric, even hedged. 2 of the 2 sessions that quote that MAPE (the 4 others of the scenario do not quote it). Known kind (causes of its own, 0.5.0).
findings.action: None required: the rule exists. If it should stop, the `MetricUnitNotice` of `mean_absolute_percentage_error` could carry the fact itself when the target has values near zero (the profile has the minimum, 1 here): the error is divided by each actual value, so the agent would quote it instead of inferring it.

findings.title: With several series, 3 of 3 agents describe the backtest as 9 folds of 14 days although the summary says the last one has 8.
findings.evidence: multi_series__r1 `9 folds of 14 days each (360 predictions in total)`, multi_series__r2 `9 consecutive 14-day windows, with 120 predictions per item`, multi_series__r3 `over 9 windows of 14 days`. `create_cv`, `backtest` and `compare` say `9 folds (the last one has only 8 steps)`. The counts they give (360, 120 per item) are right and contradict the description. With one series the short last fold is named in 10 of 13 sessions; of the 3 others, basic_forecast__noskill__r1 writes `6 folds of 12 months each, covering 62 predictions` and basic_forecast__r1 and __r3 give the folds and the 62 predictions without naming it. From 2 of 3 in `0.5.0-fix1` and `0.5.0-fix3`. Known.
findings.action: As in fix1 and fix3: none required. Now that it is 3 of 3, the summary of several series could give the predictions per series next to the folds (`120 per series: 8 folds of 14 and one of 8`).

findings.title: The agent adds a prediction interval or a list of metrics the user did not ask for.
findings.evidence: `interval=[0.1, 0.9]`: basic_forecast__r1, __r2, __r3 and basic_forecast__noskill__r1 (the request asks whether the forecast can be trusted), multi_series__r2 and __r3, foundation_default__r1, __r2 and __r3 (the request asks how accurate it is): 9 sessions. Only basic_forecast__r3 says it is its own choice (`I assumed ... an 80% interval`). A `metric` list in `compare` or `refine_plan`: basic_forecast__r1, multi_series__r2, foundation_default__r1, __r2, __r3; the plan then reads `Chosen by the user instead of the rules: metric`. Every one reports the measured coverage next to the nominal level and none presents an interval flagged by the `IntervalCoverageNotice` as 80 %, so nothing wrong reaches the user. Known (0.5.0, fix3: 3 of 3 `multi_series`).
findings.action: Low priority, as in 0.5.0: name `interval` and `metric` in the sentence of the skill on the other arguments of `plan` if it is worth stopping, or accept it for requests about trust and accuracy.

findings.title: The interval of the forecast is described from the means of its bounds in the summary, without reading the file of predictions.
findings.evidence: foundation_default__r1 `The 80% interval bounds average 0.915 (lower) and 1.088 (upper)`, __r2 `The mean of the lower bound is 0.915 and the mean of the upper bound is 1.088`, __r3 `lower bounds averaging 0.915 and upper bounds averaging 1.088 ... I only have the summary statistics above`; without the skill, basic_forecast__noskill__r1 `The mean 80% interval runs from about 0.92 to 1.09`. The skill says not to describe an interval whose file was not read; the instructions do not. The three basic_forecast sessions with the skill and multi_series__r3 read the file and give the bounds per date. 3 of 3 `foundation_default`, as 3 of 3 `user_overrides` in 0.5.0 and fix3. Known.
findings.action: As in 0.5.0, fix1 and fix3: if the rule should hold, the `<predictions>` block of a forecast of the future could leave out the statistics of the bounds or say they are not a range around the point.

findings.title: The download of the URL is denied by the client in 2 of 3 `err_url` sessions, which end without a forecast.
findings.evidence: err_url__r1 and __r3 run `D=<ws>/data/h2o; mkdir -p $D && curl -sSfL -o $D/h2o.csv <url> && ls -l $D`; the client answers `This Bash command contains multiple operations. The following part requires approval: ls -l ...` and tells the agent not to retry. Both stop, do not pass the URL to the server, and give the user the command; err_url__r2 writes the same steps without the variable, downloads and forecasts. err_url__r3 does not load the skill (the only session of 36 that has it and does not) and adds `The server rules also say not to copy or rewrite data in myself`, a rule that is about files of the user outside the directory, not about a download the user asked for. The scenario accepts asking the user, so the 3 are correct; the rate of sessions that reach the server is 1 of 3. Known limit (comment of `err_url` in `scenarios.py`).
findings.action: None in the library. In the harness, record it next to the limit of `dirty_data`: a compound command with a shell variable is asked for whatever the allowed prefixes.

findings.title: The period of the seasonal naive baseline is stated by the agent, since the summary of `compare` does not give it.
findings.evidence: basic_forecast__r2 `a seasonal-naive baseline, which repeats last year's values`, basic_forecast__r3 `that repeats the previous year`, basic_forecast__noskill__r2 `(repeat last year's values)`, basic_forecast__noskill__r3 `which repeats last year's values`. The summary says `Baseline (seasonal naive) (ForecasterEquivalentDate, repeats past values)`. In exog_no_future__r3 the period is quoted from a response (the plan of the winning baseline says 24 steps). 4 sessions, as 4 in `0.5.0-fix1`, where it was found right for this data; not reproduced in this review. Known, deferred to 0.6.0 and accepted in the log.
findings.action: As accepted for 0.6.0: give the offset of the baseline in the `comparison_overview`.

findings.title: One agent with the skill promises a comparison against the seasonal naive baseline on the data whose gaps it will leave.
findings.evidence: dirty_data_keep_gaps__r3, turn 1: `run a backtest and a comparison against the seasonal naive baseline ... The 3 missing months would still be in the data`; turn 2: `with the backtest and baseline comparison`. The skill and the instructions say there is no baseline when the target has gaps; dirty_data__r2, dirty_data__r3 and dirty_data_keep_gaps__r1 say so in their first answer (`the comparison would have no seasonal naive baseline`), and dirty_data__noskill__r2 too, from the instructions. No session runs `compare` on the copy, so the behavior itself is not reproduced here. 1 of 6 sessions with the skill.
findings.action: None: the rule is in the skill and 3 of the 6 quote it. Count the rate once the scenario gets past the copy.

findings.title: One agent names a candidate `Strategy plan`, the name the skill says no candidate can take.
findings.evidence: foundation_default__r3: `compare(candidates=[{name: 'Strategy plan', config: {}}])` answers `invalid_argument`, `The candidate name 'Strategy plan' is reserved for the plan the strategy was created for. Rename the candidate.` The agent then calls `compare` without `candidates`, which runs the 5 configurations (19 fits), and reports them right. The two other repetitions pass the Chronos-2 candidate explicitly. 1 of 3; understood at the first attempt.
findings.action: None. If it repeats, step 6 of the skill could say in so many words that the plan of the strategy needs no candidate to be compared without `candidates`.

basic_forecast__r1.notes: profile, plan, create_cv, compare (19 fits, read from `cost`), forecast of the winner and the predictions file read. The 12 values with their bounds from the file, the leaderboard, 3 of 4 beat the baseline, 13.7 % and 6.0 % attributed to the server, coverage 79 % called a rough check on few points, the Ridge intervals said to fall short, the license from the notice, no cause given. Slips: an 80 % interval and a metric list nobody asked for, and the 2-step last fold not named (it gives the 62 predictions).

basic_forecast__r2.notes: Same flow; `6 folds of 12 steps, with the last fold only 2 steps, so 62 predictions`, MASE 0.615 read against repeating the previous month, coverage 79 % as an estimate on 62 values, the bounds read from the file, license and download said. Slips: the interval nobody asked for, and the period of the baseline (`repeats last year's values`) stated by itself. `Auto-ARIMA` is the wording of the schema of `plan`.

basic_forecast__r3.notes: Same flow and figures; says it assumed the 80 % interval, MASE read against the one-step naive and `not a comparison against the seasonal baseline`, 3 of 4 beat the baseline, coverage 79 % on 62 values called rough, the drop from January to February described from the file with `I can't say why`. Slips: `6 folds of 12 steps` without the short last one (62 predictions given), baseline period stated by itself.

basic_forecast__noskill__r1.notes: Without the skill: the whole workflow with a compare, the leaderboard with MASE read against the one-step naive, 13.7 % and about 6 % from the summary, coverage 79 % and the Ridge intervals not to rely on, no error measure for the forecast said. Slips: `6 folds of 12 months each, covering 62 predictions` (the last fold has 2), the interval of the forecast described from the means of its bounds without reading the file, and an interval nobody asked for.

basic_forecast__noskill__r2.notes: Without the skill: plan with no extra argument, compare and forecast of the winner. `6 folds of up to 12 months each, 62 predictions`, the baseline beaten by the winner and two others, MASE against the one-step naive as `a different yardstick`, MAPE as about 7 %, no interval said, no hyperparameter search said. Slip: the period of the baseline stated by itself.

basic_forecast__noskill__r3.notes: Without the skill: same flow; says it did not read the predictions file and gives only the summary figures, the leaderboard with MASE read right, the 2-step last fold named, no interval requested and none described, the forecast without an error measure of its own. Slip: baseline period stated by itself.

exog_no_future__r1.notes: Plan with `use_exog: false` at once, said with the reason and an offer to rerun with the 24 rows; backtest and forecast, 27 folds and 648 predictions, MASE against repeating the previous hour and not a seasonal baseline, the negative backtest prediction named, no compare run said. But it gives a cause of its own for a metric: MAPE 168 % `is inflated by hours with very few users`, which no response says.

exog_no_future__r2.notes: `use_exog: false`, compare without candidates (25 fits): every candidate runs without the exogenous columns and Chronos-2 wins; forecast of the winner. Names the model and its license, the only one of 3 that beats the baseline with the 31.5 % of the server, says it did not open the file, that the comparison says nothing on whether the exogenous columns would help, and that no values were invented.

exog_no_future__r3.notes: `use_exog: false`, compare of LightGBM and Ridge without exogenous columns: the baseline wins and the agent forecasts with it, saying so (`neither machine-learning model beat the seasonal naive baseline`). The period of 24 hours comes from the plan of the winner. Exogenous columns left out said, no interval said, nothing invented.

exog_no_future__noskill__r1.notes: Without the skill: `use_exog: false` and a forecast with no backtest. It follows both notices: says the forecast has no accuracy measure and is not to be treated as reliable yet, and that the three columns were left out because their future values are missing and it does not make them up. Notes that the predicted mean is far below the historical one without giving a cause.

exog_no_future__noskill__r2.notes: Without the skill: same as r1. No backtest; says it cannot say how accurate the forecast is and offers one, says the exogenous columns are ignored and why, and that the predictions are much lower than the historical average, with no cause.

exog_no_future__noskill__r3.notes: Without the skill: `use_exog: false`, backtest and forecast; 27 folds and 648 predictions, MASE against the previous hour and no claim on a seasonal baseline, negative backtest predictions named, exogenous columns left out said. But MAPE 168 % `is inflated by hours with very low user counts` is a cause of its own, against rule 7 of the instructions.

multi_series__r1.notes: profile without target (the request says sales, the file has `value`), then target and `series_id_column`; backtest, compare, the metrics per series of the winner read from the file, forecast with Chronos-2 (named, with its license). Per item MAE, RMSE, MASE and MAPE as a percentage, item_2 the weakest, no baseline with several series said, MASE against the previous day. Slip: `9 folds of 14 days each`, missing the last fold of 8 days.

multi_series__r2.notes: Same flow with a `refine_plan` that adds an 80 % interval and a metric list nobody asked for. Per item metrics and coverage (82.5 %, 85 %, 85 %) from the file, called a rough check on 120 values, the bounds not described, item_2 the least reliable, `the server doesn't offer` a baseline for several series (right, unlike fix3 r2). Slip: `9 consecutive 14-day windows`.

multi_series__r3.notes: Same flow with an interval nobody asked for; reads the metrics and the predictions files and gives five dates with their bounds, the coverage and the width per item, item_2 the weakest, LightGBM not used because of its coverage (27.5 % to 35 %), no seasonal baseline for several series. Says what it assumed about the columns. Slip: `9 windows of 14 days`.

compare_code__r1.notes: compare, `get_code` of the comparison (the backtest script) and then of `links.best_plan_id`. Leaderboard, 3 of 4 beat the baseline, the 2-step last fold and 62 predictions, the 6.0 % of the summary, license, forecast not run said. The script handed with one change it names (the path), and the requirements exactly as the tool gives them (`pandas==2.3.3 skforecast==0.27.0 chronos-forecasting==2.3.2`).

compare_code__r2.notes: compare, forecast of the winner and `get_code` of its plan. Folds with the short last one, 3 of 4 beat the baseline, 62 predictions, the forecast range from the summary without an error measure, license, the script unchanged with the requirements of the response. Wording slip: the opening says the five models were compared `on the 12 months after the end of the data`, which the next section corrects (a backtest).

compare_code__r3.notes: compare and `get_code` of the winner. Leaderboard, the 2-step last fold, 62 predictions, 3 of 4 beat the baseline, 13.7 % and 6.0 % attributed to the server, MASE against the one-step naive and not the seasonal baseline, no forecast run and no interval said, license, the script unchanged and the requirements exactly as given.

err_url__r1.notes: Never passes the URL to the server. Its download command (`D=...; mkdir -p $D && curl ... && ls -l $D`) is denied by the client, which also says not to retry; it stops, says what was blocked, gives the user the command and says it has not seen the data, so `x` and the monthly frequency are still assumptions. No forecast: limit of the harness, the scenario accepts asking the user.

err_url__r2.notes: Downloads into `data/h2o/` with the allowed command and says where, then profile, plan, backtest, forecast and the predictions file. The 12 values, `6 folds of up to 12 steps each, covering 62 predictions`, MAPE as 7.2 %, MASE against the one-step naive and nothing about a seasonal one, no compare run and no interval said.

err_url__r3.notes: Does not load the skill and starts with the download, which the client denies (same command form as r1). Never passes the URL; says no forecast ran and gives the user the two commands. Slip: `The server rules also say not to copy or rewrite data in myself`, which is the rule for files outside the directory, not for the download the user asked for.

err_outside_dir__r1.notes: Builds the path inside the allowed directory, meets `data_not_found` once and stops: the server only reads under `data`, it may not copy or move the file, and the user can copy it there or restart with `--allow-dir`. No search outside, no retry.

err_outside_dir__r2.notes: Same as r1: one `data_not_found`, the allowed directory named, the two options for the user, nothing copied. Says it assumes 12 months means 12 observations.

err_outside_dir__r3.notes: Same as r1, plus one `Glob` inside `data` to confirm the file is not there. Explains the directory rule and the two options, copies nothing.

err_bad_target__r1.notes: Passes `sales` as written, meets the error and asks: the file has `fecha` and `x`, and it will not assume that `x` is the sales figure. Nothing else runs.

err_bad_target__r2.notes: Same as r1: one error, the two real columns named, a question before using `x`.

err_bad_target__r3.notes: Same as r1: one error, the columns named, `I don't want to guess which column you meant`.

err_long_horizon__r1.notes: profile, then `plan` with 120 steps as asked: `invalid_argument` on `steps`. Explains the limit of 60 observations, asks which horizon and offers examples (12, 24, a longer history) without choosing one. No forecast run.

err_long_horizon__r2.notes: Same as r1; suggests 12 or 24 months and asks, says nothing ran, and that a longer history must be copied into `data` by the user.

err_long_horizon__r3.notes: Same as r1: `I haven't picked a different horizon for you`, the limit explained, two options offered.

dirty_data__r1.notes: Inconclusive: the client denies `sed '91d' h2o_dirty.csv > h2o_clean.csv` after the user agreed, so no copy, no profile and no forecast. What can be judged is right: turn 1 names the three problems, says the server does not fill missing values and asks before writing, with nothing written or read; in turn 2 it inspects the file read-only, says honestly that nothing was written and the original is untouched, says what the copy would hold (the first `2006-01-01` row kept, the gaps left) and gives the command. Does not try `Write`.

dirty_data__r2.notes: Inconclusive: the client denies the `awk ... > h2o_clean.csv` of turn 2. Turn 1 names the three problems, says the gaps would stay and that a comparison would then have no seasonal naive baseline (from the skill), and asks for the rule of the repeated date. Turn 2 says nothing was written, that keeping the first row of each date removes both repeats and leaves the 3 gaps, and gives the command. Does not try `Write`.

dirty_data__r3.notes: Inconclusive: in turn 2 it writes a script under `/tmp` with a here-document, denied whole. Turn 1 names the three problems and asks, saying the server will warn about the gaps and skip the baseline. Turn 2 says the command was denied, nothing was written and neither file changed, and describes what the script would have done (first row of each date kept, gaps left). Wording slip: `The command ran a short Python script`, corrected by the sentences around it. Does not try `Write`.

dirty_data__noskill__r1.notes: Inconclusive: without the skill, `sed '91d' ... > h2o_dedup.csv` is denied in turn 2. Turn 1 names the three problems and asks three questions (the repeated date, the identical row, the gaps) before writing. Turn 2 says nothing was written, which line stays and which goes, that the identical row and the 3 gaps stay as asked, and gives the command.
